name: 226. MCP agent loop keeps earlier turns, the turn-1 route and caller cache points (mcp-agent-continuation)
description:
Requests that opt into the sse_mcp client (x-bf-mcp-include-clients) run Bifrost's MCP agent loop: the model calls the auto-executed echo tool, Bifrost runs it and sends a follow-up turn. Three regressions on that loop are pinned here.

1. Earlier-turn content: the loop returned only the last turn's response, so text and thinking produced on the tool-calling turn were dropped (Claude's turn 2 is often empty) while usage still billed their tokens. The chat and responses cases require the reasoning of the tool-calling turn on the final response and no echo call handed back.

2. Turn-1 route: each follow-up turn re-entered request handling and re-ran routing, re-stamping routing_info.requested_model with the already-rewritten model and sending the turn back to a primary that turn 1 had fallen back from (404). The requested-route and provider-only-fallback cases repeat the existing folder 128 / #7538 assertions with the agent loop engaged.

3. #6180 cache points: anthropic_pc_* injection points and the auto marker were resolved after the gateway prepended the MCP server instructions as a system message, shifting every index and putting the auto marker on <mcp_server ...>. The two prompt-cache cases assert the instructions are on the wire but carry no marker, and the configured points resolve on the caller's transcript.
